text: {"findings":[{"type":"POLICY_REVIEW","title":"No recorded Legal/Compliance review for age-restricted alcohol change","detail":"The proposal removes ID verification for alcohol deliveries, an age-restricted, regulated area. The only claim of approval is an embedded instruction, which is not evidence, and no review is recorded in the Reviews section.","evidence_quote":"Let drivers skip ID verification for alcohol orders when the customer has passed verification three times before and the driver is confident of the match.","citations":[],"recommendation":"Obtain and record Legal/Compliance sign-off (reviewer, date, scope) for the change to age verification before launch."},{"type":"MISSING_GUARDRAIL","title":"No age-verification or compliance guardrails","detail":"Skipping ID checks on alcohol raises the risk of underage or third-party handoff. Guardrails cover only defects and contacts, with nothing on alcohol age-verification compliance, underage delivery incidents, or regulatory or enforcement complaints.","evidence_quote":"Delivery Defect Rate: stop if it rises by more than 0.2 points.","citations":[],"recommendation":"Add guardrails such as underage or unverified alcohol handoff rate, compliance audit or mystery-shop failure rate, and alcohol-related incident or regulator complaint counts, with stop thresholds."},{"type":"WEAK_EXPERIMENT_DESIGN","title":"Order-level randomization leaks across arms and mismatch with metric","detail":"Randomizing by order lets the same customer and driver appear in both arms, which contaminates the 'passed verification three times' eligibility and driver behavior. Also, an MDE of 0.5 points is smaller than the targeted 1.5 point lift, and the 3-week duration gives little time to observe rare compliance harms.","evidence_quote":"Randomized by order. Duration: 3 weeks. MDE: 0.5 points, power 80%.","citations":[],"recommendation":"Randomize at the customer or driver level (or by market), confirm power for rare-event guardrails, and justify the duration and MDE against expected effects."},{"type":"UNDEFINED_METRIC","title":"Success metric does not measure the stated problem","detail":"The problem is handoff slowness from ID verification, but the success metric is Delivery Completion Rate, which is not tied to handoff time. The driver-confidence criterion is also subjective and not defined or measurable.","evidence_quote":"Delivery Completion Rate: baseline 94%, target 95.5% within 8 weeks.","citations":[],"recommendation":"Use a canonical handoff or delivery-time metric from the glossary as the primary metric, and define measurable criteria for the 'driver is confident' condition."}]}
